summary: This note is the Snowflake reference page for the SPLIT_PART string function, which splits a string at a specified delimiter and returns the requested part. It covers the syntax and arguments, usage notes on out-of-range, negative, and zero part numbers, empty delimiters, and collation restrictions, followed by several examples showing the behavior.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the SPLIT_PART string function, which returns a chosen part of a delimiter-split string.
key_facts: SPLIT_PART(<string>, <delimiter>, <partNumber>) splits a given string at a specified character and returns the requested part.
If any parameter of SPLIT_PART is NULL, NULL is returned.
The partNumber argument is 1-based, and a negative partNumber counts parts backward from the end of the string.
If partNumber is out of range, SPLIT_PART returns an empty string.
If partNumber is 0, it is treated as 1, and Snowflake recommends avoiding 0 as a synonym for 1.
If the separator is an empty string, the returned value is the input string because the string is not split.
SPLIT_PART does not support the pi (punctuation-insensitive) collation specification or the cs-ai (case-sensitive, accent-insensitive) collation specification.
Using SPLIT_PART with a column that has the upper or lower collation specifiers requires enabling the 2024_02 behavior change bundle via SYSTEM$ENABLE_BEHAVIOR_CHANGE_BUNDLE('2024_02').
For SPLIT_PART('|a|b|c|', '|', 1) the result is an empty string, because the leading separator makes an empty first element.
SPLIT_PART('aaa--bbb-BBB--ccc', '--', 2) returns bbb-BBB, showing a multi-character separator.
If the string starts or ends with the delimiter, the empty space before or after it counts as a valid part of the split result.
